title: Building Institutional Trust in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Workforce Development Strategies for Technology Adoption
text_snippet: Building Institutional Trust in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Workforce Development Strategies for Technology Adoption The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizational work processes has created opportunities for improved efficiency, decision support, and workforce capability. Still, it has also intensified employee concerns about job security, skill relevance, surveillance, fairness, and leadership transparency. These concerns can weaken institutional trust and reduce employee engagement when AI implementation is framed primarily as a technical rollout rather than a workforce development challenge. This conceptual article synthesizes research on organizational trust, employee engagement, AI adoption, psychological safety, and workforce development to examine how organizations can sustain trust during AI-enabled transformation. The article argues that successful AI implementation depends on four trust-building practices: continuous workforce training, transparent communication from leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and structured feedback mechanisms. title: Future Forecasts? - Is AI a Workforce Revolution or Disruption?
text_snippet: Future Forecasts? - Is AI a Workforce Revolution or Disruption? This narrative literature review synthesizes findings from research studies, publications from 2024 to 2026, and AI-generated prompts to examine forecasts of how artificial intelligence (AI) may affect the workforce. The literature consistently showed that AI is transforming job structures, automating routine tasks, and changing skill requirements. Information-based and cognitive roles appear most vulnerable to automation, while physically intensive and interpersonal jobs are less affected. At the same time, new employment categories are emerging in AI development, digital transformation, human-AI collaboration, and data-driven decision support. The literature also raises concerns about job displacement among low-skill workers, widening inequality, the need for large-scale retraining, regulatory safeguards, and the continued importance of human-driven innovation. Overall, scholars, practitioners, and leaders suggest that AI is more likely to augment, rather than fully replacing human labor. Although AI’s long-term impact on the workforce remains uncertain, its influence is undeniable as organizations adapt to rapidly evolving technological capabilities.

title: What Can We Learn About AI from Leaders and Entrepreneurs?
text_snippet: What Can We Learn About AI from Leaders and Entrepreneurs? This article introduces the University of Phoenix Center for Leadership and Entrepreneurial Research | AI Lab (CLER | AI Lab), a new initiative examining artificial intelligence through the lived experiences of leaders and entrepreneurs. Grounded in scholar-practitioner principles, the lab explores four interconnected areas: AIinformed leadership decision-making; entrepreneurial innovation and AI adoption among small and mid-sized organizations; ethical, responsible, and inclusive AI governance; and organizational learning and workforce readiness. Drawing on emerging research, the lab seeks to bridge theory and practice, advancing evidencebased approaches that help organizations navigate AI transformation responsibly. As AI reshapes leadership, identity, equity, and the future of work. The CLER | AI Lab positions scholar-practitioners to contribute rigorous, timely insights that inform AI policy, practice, and education. title: The Spark: What Entrepreneurs Teach Us About Artificial Intelligence, a Narrative Inquiry
text_snippet: The Spark: What Entrepreneurs Teach Us About Artificial Intelligence, a Narrative Inquiry Entrepreneurs are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) as both a creative partner and an operational resource. However, a semantic review of 50 studies, published between 2024 and 2026 revealed that existing scholarships have focused primarily on AI adoption in education and business enterprises, leaving limited understanding of how individual entrepreneurs use AI to generate ideas, innovate, and build new ventures. To address this gap, this study involved purposeful sampling with a podcast-based interview format to collect and analyze entrepreneurial AI experiences. Using narrative inquiry, investigators examined the lived experience of one entrepreneur—Ron—whose AI journey began with a question at a shooting range. In fewer than four months, Ron’s collaboration and communication with his ChatGPT named “Homie” helped him to produce a patented product, a published book, a website, and an operational business. His narrative illustrates how entrepreneurial engagement with AI can support venture development through prompting, iterative questioning, contextual refinement, and collaborative problem-solving. title: Staying Power in STEM Teaching: A Mixed-Methods Study of Elementary Teachers' Self-Efficacy, Burnout, and Barriers to Sustaining STEM Instruction
text_snippet: Staying Power in STEM Teaching: A Mixed-Methods Study of Elementary Teachers' Self-Efficacy, Burnout, and Barriers to Sustaining STEM Instruction This mixed-methods descriptive study examined in-service elementary STEM teachers about their experience in their roles, preparation, stressors, and supports, with particular attention to teacher self-efficacy, burnout risk, and workplace attrition pressures. Using Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, we explored the four sources of self-efficacy as mediators that influence teacher resilience and sustainability in STEM teaching roles. Eleven teachers completed a well-established and validated questionnaire (T-STEM) using Likert-scale efficacy items and reported on classroom practices through open-ended reflections. Reliability of scale and subscales were calculated using Cronbach’s alpha. Quantitative data were summarized by subscale means and a composite self-efficacy score. title: Shaping Career Momentum: Leadership in Action During Performance Calibration Cycles
text_snippet: Shaping Career Momentum: Leadership in Action During Performance Calibration Cycles Performance calibration processes are commonly designed to ensure consistency in employee evaluation and advancement decisions. However, these recurring discussions function as leadership systems through which organizations translate performance narratives into signals about opportunity, recognition, and career progression. This paper examines performance calibration cycles as structurally embedded decision environments that shape career momentum, institutional trust, and leadership pipelines. Drawing on research in organizational justice, managerial accountability, psychosocial work environments, and moral decisionmaking, the analysis explains how time pressure, comparative evaluation, and incomplete information can compress judgment within calibration settings. Over repeated cycles, small interpretive differences accumulate into structural patterns influencing career advancement and perceptions of fairness across organizations. When calibration systems incorporate transparent criteria, evidence-based reviews, and distributed accountability, they can moderate interpretive distortion and strengthen institutional credibility. title: Book Review - The Trusted Learning Advisor: The Tools, Techniques and Skills You Need to Make L&D a Business Priority
text_snippet: Book Review - The Trusted Learning Advisor: The Tools, Techniques and Skills You Need to Make L&D a Business Priority This review examines Keith Keating’s book The Trusted Learning Advisor and its implications for the evolving role of Learning and Development (L&D) professionals in contemporary organizations. The book argues that L&D practitioners must move beyond the traditional role of training providers and instead operate as strategic advisors capable of diagnosing business problems and aligning learning solutions with organizational goals. Drawing on Keating’s professional experience and frameworks such as the Intake, Discovery, Analysis, and Decision (IDAD) model, the text presents practical strategies for building credibility with stakeholders and demonstrating the business value of learning initiatives. The book also addresses the growing influence of artificial intelligence and the changing skills required of learning professionals in technology-driven workplaces. This review evaluates the book’s contributions to both practice and theory and considers its relevance for leaders seeking to strengthen organizational learning cultures.

title: Mindfulness and Resilience in Higher Education: Concepts, Consequences, and Best Practices Recommendations
text_snippet: Mindfulness and Resilience in Higher Education: Concepts, Consequences, and Best Practices Recommendations In recent years there has been a great increase in the amount of academic and professional literature focusing on the benefits of an attitude of mindfulness and resilience. In higher education, an embrace of these concepts can create a place where faculty and students are “present, focused and capable of the kind of thinking that education requires” (Misha, 2026, para. 12). This article, aligned conceptually with Construal Level Theory, offers a brief review and summary of academic and professional works affirming the beneficial practices of mindfulness and resilience. Five recommendations are presented for applying mindfulness and resilience in the higher education environment. The recommendations are especially applicable to online programs that are often found to be deficient in terms of faculty engagement and student satisfaction with learning (Schwartz, 2020).

title: AI, Autonomy, and Institutional Trust: Cultivating Workforce Engagement in the Era of Intelligent Work
text_snippet: AI, Autonomy, and Institutional Trust: Cultivating Workforce Engagement in the Era of Intelligent Work Burnout and disengagement are frequently explained through the Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) model, which holds that sustained job demands combined with insufficient resources predict strain and reduced well-being, with inadequate recovery deepening negative outcomes (Bakker & Demerouti, 2017; Sonnentag, 2018). Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping task structures and skill requirements across industries (Brynjolfsson et al., 2023; Huang & Rust, 2021), and awareness of AI’s impact can heighten employment-risk perception, particularly among workers who lack adaptive confidence (Liang & Zhai, 2025). Because trust in AI systems and in institutional decision-making shapes acceptance of technological integration (Glikson & Woolley, 2020), and because sustainable-career scholarship ties long-term employability to ongoing development and organizational support (De Vos et al., 2020), this article argues that structured AI upskilling—implemented through autonomy-supportive practices—can strengthen workforce engagement and institutional trust.

title: Trauma-Informed Care in Alternative Education Settings: Educators' Lived Experiences
text_snippet: Trauma-Informed Care in Alternative Education Settings: Educators' Lived Experiences Alternative education settings disproportionately serve Black and Brown adolescents who experience high rates of trauma associated with poverty, community violence, housing instability, and systemic racism. Although trauma-informed care (TIC) has received increasing attention within educational research, limited scholarship has examined how educators in alternative education settings experience and implement TIC in practice. Consequently, TIC implementation remains inconsistent, leaving educators to address complex student needs without sufficient training, resources, or systemic support. This manuscript draws on a qualitative, exploratory case study using purposive sampling to recruit 17 educators, administrators, and social workers across the greater Washington, D.C., metropolitan area who had direct experience implementing TIC in alternative education settings. Six themes emerged: challenges in implementing TIC, positive behavioral and academic transformations, effective practices, integration with traditional methods, the evolution of TIC over time, and stakeholder perceptions of students. title: A Systems-Level Framework for Autonomy, Trust, and Workforce Engagement in AI-Enabled Organizations
text_snippet: A Systems-Level Framework for Autonomy, Trust, and Workforce Engagement in AI-Enabled Organizations The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizational systems is transforming work design, decisionmaking processes, and employee experiences across contemporary workplaces. Although worker autonomy, institutional trust, and workforce engagement have been widely studied within organizational research, these constructs are often examined in isolation, limiting understanding of how they interact within AI-enabled environments. This article proposes a systems-level conceptual framework in which AI integration influences employee autonomy, which in turn shapes institutional trust and subsequently workforce engagement. The framework conceptualizes AI as both enabling and constraining employee autonomy depending on how technological systems are designed and implemented within organizations. Grounded in socio-technical systems theory and self-determination theory, the framework further reconceptualizes institutional trust as a dual-target construct encompassing trust in both organizational leadership and algorithmic systems. title: Psychological Capital as a Foundation for Career Optimism: A Strategic Integration of Research and Contemporary Workforce Insights
text_snippet: Psychological Capital as a Foundation for Career Optimism: A Strategic Integration of Research and Contemporary Workforce Insights This paper explores Psychological Capital (PsyCap) as a crucial foundation for career optimism, integrating scholarly research with contemporary workforce insights from the 2025 Career Optimism Index®. PsyCap, comprised of hope, optimism, resilience, and self-efficacy, is presented as a developable resource that enhances individual adaptability, motivation, and performance. The paper demonstrates how PsyCap fosters workforce readiness, student success, and organizational stability by bridging the gap between career aspirations and actual capabilities. Core components such as hope and optimism drive goal pursuit and confidence, while resilience and self-efficacy support adaptability and proactive growth. Empirical evidence shows that higher PsyCap is linked to increased engagement, retention, and reduced stress, benefiting both employees and organizations. By embedding PsyCap development into talent management and workforce strategies, institutions can cultivate a resilient, optimistic, and future-ready workforce prepared to thrive amid ongoing change and uncertainty. title: Encyclopedic or Metagogical? Two Postures for AI in a Workforce Facing a Crisis of Trust
text_snippet: Encyclopedic or Metagogical? Two Postures for AI in a Workforce Facing a Crisis of Trust The 2025 Career Optimism Index documents an American workforce in crisis — record-high burnout, autonomy collapse, and an unprecedented turn toward artificial intelligence as a tool for skill development and resilience. This essay argues that the institutional question for 2026 is not whether to adopt AI but in whose service it is held. Two postures are named: encyclopedic, in which the tool replaces practitioner judgment, and metagogical, in which the tool extends it. The article draws on the metagogy framework (McCaslin & Scott, 2012), names the trust-building mechanism that distinguishes the two postures, locates what is at stake for the ScholarPractitioner-Leader (McCaslin, 2013), and offers a concrete instance from doctoral teaching practice. The argument is that institutional trust is built or eroded at the level of posture, not at the level of adoption. The distinction is defined here as a construct, and the claim is framed so that it can be tested.

title: Benefits and Risks of Inclusion for Preschool Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Qualitative Multi-case Study
text_snippet: Benefits and Risks of Inclusion for Preschool Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Qualitative Multi-case Study Early childhood education has been influenced by various theories on child development, impacting practices for both typically and atypically developing children. Educational pioneers argue that children with special needs should have access to the general education curriculum with necessary modifications. With the increasing number of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in preschool, equitable opportunities must address individual needs through constructivist approaches that recognize the link between language, cognitive, and social-emotional development in the least restrictive environment (LRE). The joint policy by the U.S. Departments of Health and Human Services and Education emphasizes the benefits of inclusive classroom settings, yet significant barriers to implementation persist. This case study explored the methods preschool teachers use to support children with ASD and their reasons for selecting those strategies. Results indicate a need for professional development and stronger collaboration between private childcare centers and public schools to implement the joint policy effectively.

title: Leadership management and succession planning
text_snippet: Leadership management and succession planning Succession Planning and Development is nothing new. However, an organization’s productivity and retention effectiveness are highly dependent on implementing a meaningful succession plan and evaluating its effectiveness. Whether business-centered or public agencies, organizations exist in an extremely competitive environment in this age of fast-moving initiatives and employee job-searching. Technology is rapidly impacting the workforce, making quality staffing difficult to sustain. To bolster a productive and satisfied workforce, leaders and managers must be educated, empowered, and mentored in the requisite skills and experience. The concept of succession development is also referred to as talent management, which is how the plan develops future leaders and managers to fill a talent pool ready for promotional placement at any moment. Preparing talented staff to fill leader vacancies in advance is much more beneficial to the organization than reacting to a short-notice vacancy need and not being ready to fill that vacancy quickly and effectively.

title: Exploring the challenges of managing remote employees within federal agencies
text_snippet: Exploring the challenges of managing remote employees within federal agencies The evolution of technology has redefined workforce talent development, particularly in organizations struggling to optimize communication technology to foster collaboration, engagement, and productivity. This has created a critical role for advanced communication technology in navigating the evolving landscape of developing dynamic workforce talent from within. This study explores how effective information communication technology (ICT) can optimize workforce performance, enhance collaboration, and foster innovation among teleworking employees. This research used a qualitative appreciative inquiry approach to identify five key strategies to improve telework efficiency: optimizing communication tools, overcoming management challenges, harnessing artificial intelligence for operational efficiency, overcoming barriers to technology adoption, and enhancing teleworking management. These findings offer scholar-practitioner leaders and policymakers actionable strategies and data-driven insights for bridging technology gaps to cultivate agile, high-performing, resilient remote teams and adaptable remote workforce talent development in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

title: Developing dynamic workforce talent with gen z and millennials
text_snippet: Developing dynamic workforce talent with gen z and millennials By 2025, Millennials and members of Generation Z will represent a significant proportion of the global workforce, reshaping workplace cultures, expectations, and talent development strategies. These generations consistently prioritize purpose-driven work, flexibility, continuous learning, and inclusive environments. At the same time, organizations face pressing challenges, including bridging generational differences, balancing flexibility with necessary structure, and addressing evolving understandings of purpose and mental well-being. Critical skills gaps also persist in both technical and interpersonal domains. Employers report high demand for expertise in data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and software development, alongside essential soft skills such as communication, critical thinking, adaptability, and leadership. To meet these needs, organizations must implement personalized learning pathways, mentorship programs, continuous feedback mechanisms, and advanced technology-driven solutions for professional development. title: Retention and professional growth: A dual approach to strengthening the teaching workforce
text_snippet: Retention and professional growth: A dual approach to strengthening the teaching workforce Teacher retention and professional development are important factors influencing teacher growth and development. The role of principals in developing a school culture that supports both teacher retention and career-long growth is critical. Research highlights that structured mentorship programs, targeted professional development, and shared decision-making processes contribute significantly to teacher satisfaction and professional growth. Effective leadership creates an environment where educators feel valued, supported, and motivated to refine their instructional practices. Furthermore, establishing policies that promote collaboration, trust, and professional learning advances teachers’ sense of connectedness in their schools. As younger generations enter the teaching profession with shifting career expectations, school leaders must provide personalized growth opportunities to grow and keep the best teachers. By prioritizing mentorship, professional learning, and recognition, principals can not only reduce teacher attrition but also promote a thriving environment where both teachers and students can achieve maximum growth advancements.

title: From battlefield to boardroom: Leveraging military healthcare leadership for workforce talent development
text_snippet: From battlefield to boardroom: Leveraging military healthcare leadership for workforce talent development By encouraging flexibility, crisis management, and organized leadership development, military healthcare leadership offers a strong foundation for workforce talent development. The framework for civilian workforce development examined in this paper is military healthcare leadership, with particular attention paid to skill development, talent stagnation, and military-to-corporate migrations. This research highlights obstacles and effective practices for integrating military-trained professionals into leadership roles by examining career trajectories from the military to the civilian sector. Drawing on five primary sources, such as studies on leadership empowerment, human resource management, and military medicine, the study emphasizes the value of mission-oriented decision-making, multidisciplinary collaboration, and organized training in improving organizational performance. Companies and educators may use military leadership concepts to create a workforce that is resilient and productive. The discussion of workforce development, leadership flexibility, and the changing needs of the contemporary labor market is enhanced by these observations.

title: From the inside out: A theoretical framework for whole person development in an AI-driven workforce
text_snippet: From the inside out: A theoretical framework for whole person development in an AI-driven workforce As the workforce evolves amid the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), organizations must shift from outdated development models to intentional strategies that cultivate dynamic internal talent. This theoretical essay presents a framework rooted in Carl Jung’s concept of synchronicity and Albert Bandura’s social cognitive theory of self-efficacy for AI integration with learning and development processes. The proposed model uses a triangle symbolizing vision, spirituality, and physical well-being, with a heart at its center representing intention (thoughts and behaviors of the individual). This whole-person development model supports employee engagement, inspires personalized leadership and learning, and helps organizations build a culture of continuous learning that combats talent stagnation and promotes purposeful internal growth.

title: Cognitive bias, emotion regulation, and leaders’ mental health: implications for leadership
text_snippet: Cognitive bias, emotion regulation, and leaders’ mental health: implications for leadership Societal shifts in the post-COVID-19 era have had profound implications for communities at large, posing significant challenges to leadership adaptability, mental health, and the sustainability of effective leadership in navigating an abrupt and unfamiliar new normal. Critical thinking has become essential in enabling national leaders to address urgent issues across diverse sectors in this evolving context. The present era calls for leadership that is informed, impartial, and grounded in objectivity. This theoretical essay examines how cognitive biases, emotional regulation, and the deterioration of leaders’ mental health may influence decision-making in high-stakes and routine scenarios. Furthermore, it explores research-based recommendations to support leaders in responding effectively to these complex demands.

title: Empowering self-concepts for self-leadership: Developing dynamic workforce talent from within
text_snippet: Empowering self-concepts for self-leadership: Developing dynamic workforce talent from within As explained in Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory (1977) the concept of agency involves ownership and control over internal thoughts and external actions. Therefore, self is a cognitive concept that encompasses beliefs, regulation, discipline, determination, and care (Bandura, 1977). This is what guides self-leadership. The self-concept scenarios, in this discourse, are offered to provide practical applications for team leaders to encourage self-leadership when the goal is to develop a dynamic workforce suitable for today’s dynamic workplace.

title: Bridging the divide: Understanding the relationship between generation gaps and talent stagnation in the workforce
text_snippet: Bridging the divide: Understanding the relationship between generation gaps and talent stagnation in the workforce Generational differences in the workplace, spanning Baby Boomers, Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z, significantly impact organizational dynamics, collaboration, and employee engagement. Variations in work ethics, communication styles, technology proficiency, and career development expectations among these cohorts often lead to misunderstandings, diminished teamwork, and talent stagnation. This paper examines how contrasting generational perspectives—such as Baby Boomers’ hierarchical and loyalty-driven approach, Generation X’s independence and flexibility preference, Millennials’ collaborative and purpose-driven ethos, and Generation Z’s entrepreneurial and digitally fluent mindset—contribute to workplace misalignment. Additionally, disparities in communication norms, from traditional formal interactions favored by older generations to informal digital exchanges preferred by younger employees, further complicate cross-generational collaboration. Organizations face challenges in technology adoption, leadership succession, and limited career advancement opportunities, disproportionately affecting employee morale and retention. title: A comparative analysis of the use of LEAN and door-to-needed times in stroke centers
text_snippet: A comparative analysis of the use of LEAN and door-to-needed times in stroke centers This study investigated the impact of LEAN methodologies on door-to-needle (DTN) times in acute stroke centers. Data from 44 centers in the American Heart Association’s Get with the Guidelines registry were analyzed, comparing 23 LEAN-utilizing centers with 21 non-LEAN centers. Independent sample t tests revealed that centers employing LEAN achieved significantly better mean DTN percentages (90.61%) compared to those not using LEAN (78.95%), t(32.37) = 1.98, p = .028, with a moderate effect size (g = 0.611). While post hoc chi-square analyses of ranked data were nonsignificant, the findings suggested that LEAN methodologies are associated with improved timely delivery of thrombolytic medication for acute stroke patients, potentially leading to better outcomes. Further research with larger samples is warranted.

title: How authentic leaders confront fear and build trust during workplace crisis
text_snippet: How authentic leaders confront fear and build trust during workplace crisis The problem is that leaders who fail to manage their fears while leading often resort to shortcuts that may command attention but lack genuine influence, which can have detrimental effects on the organization and individuals in leadership roles. In today’s volatile and complex organizational environments, fear remains an underexplored yet influential factor in leadership practice. When mismanaged, fear can lead to destructive behaviors such as micromanagement, intimidation, and manipulation, which erode psychological safety and hinder employee well-being, innovation, and trust. This theoretical essay explores the relationship between fear, leadership behavior, and psychological safety, emphasizing the critical role of authentic leadership in transforming fear into a constructive force. Authentic leaders grounded in transparency, self-awareness, and integrity are uniquely positioned to navigate fear ethically while fostering psychologically safe and high-performing work environments. Authentic leadership offers a framework for navigating fear constructively through courage, perseverance, and resilience, traits essential for ethical decision-making and relational trust. title: Improving the organizational workforce through adaptive leadership styles, emotional intelligence, and motivational language
text_snippet: Improving the organizational workforce through adaptive leadership styles, emotional intelligence, and motivational language A company’s workforce is an essential variable that companies must address to have consistency in the organization. Organizations have inconsistencies with their workforce, and addressing this need helps improve the company’s structure and culture. The inconsistencies have led to employee retention, engagement, performance, and motivational issues. Consistency allows the company to accomplish objectives and develop its staff. Emotional intelligence, leadership styles, and motivational language are the tools that can help organizations improve job satisfaction and motivation while properly engaging their staff. Organizational leaders must create a strategy encompassing emotional intelligence, leadership styles, and motivational language to meet the needs of the businesses and their staff. Company leaders who understand these variables can create a positive culture that meets their staff’s needs.

title: Empowering workforce potential through effective leadership education
text_snippet: Empowering workforce potential through effective leadership education This theoretical paper delves into the essential role of leadership education in empowering workforce potential through a holistic andragogical approach. Drawing on established leadership theories and research, it emphasizes the integration of both curricular and co-curricular contexts, specifically tailored for scholars, practitioners, and leaders. The paper highlights transformational leadership principles where leaders inspire followers to align with shared values and aspirations. It addresses the transformative capacities of leadership education, aiming to cultivate human potential beyond traditional knowledge transfer, and explores the intersection of knowledge, human potential, and experiential learning. Through a review of related scholarship, key concepts such as transformational and servant leadership are discussed. The notion of potentiating leadership, characterized by self-awareness and a focus on growth, is introduced, suggesting that effective leaders prioritize the development of their followers’ potential. The paper ultimately posits that leadership rooted in understanding human potential is crucial for fostering meaningful engagement and growth within organizations

title: Investigating the connection between soft skills and employability in IT
text_snippet: Investigating the connection between soft skills and employability in IT The demand for valuable soft skills is steadily increasing in the ever-evolving landscape of information technology (IT). While technical skills remain a prerequisite, employers seek candidates who can demonstrate essential soft skills such as effective communication, critical thinking, time management, and problem-solving abilities. This paper delves into the shifting employability criteria in IT, which now necessitate a blend of technical and soft skills to bridge the widening employment gap. The paper also aims to identify the soft skills contributing to this gap, resources for skill development, and methods to effectively communicate and advocate for these skills to secure entry-level positions or career advancement within IT.

title: Transformative Inquiry
text_snippet: Transformative Inquiry Transformative Inquiry is an approach toward understanding and fostering the full range of deep and meaningful relationships from the personal to the political and beyond. It is an integral model designed to support investigation into the essential and meaningful relationships that both transform and potentiate. Understanding the nature of human potential requires the adoption of an open perspective. Our highest aspirations demand care, consideration, and clarity of purpose. Equally important is the need for patience and understanding – from ourselves and others. Discussing Transformative inquiry reveals that the full actualization of human potential has fallen victim to the bifurcation of research methodologies. Transformative Inquiry is distinct from other approaches through its structure and content. It is a specific and unique combination of the axiological, ontological, epistemological, methodological, and rhetorical components upon which it is based.
